title: How to prepare an office fit-out budget in Australia
excerpt: A scope-led approach to fit-out budgeting that separates assumptions, project costs and evidence before a commitment is made.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Office Fit-Out Budget Guide Australia | YOS
metaDescription: Prepare an Australian office fit-out budget by defining the premises, workplace brief, scope, assumptions, programme and evidence required.
body:
## Treat the first number as a planning assumption

Early fit-out figures help a business test options. They are not quotes and should not be presented as current market facts without a dated source and defined scope.

## Define the premises and brief

Record the location, area, existing condition, building requirements and landlord works. Add the workplace needs: people, rooms, technology, accessibility, storage, furniture and operational date.

## Structure the budget

Separate professional advice, approvals, construction, mechanical and electrical services, fire, data, audio-visual, furniture, relocation and contingency. Show exclusions and GST treatment.

## Verify what moves the number

Layout complexity, existing services, acoustic requirements, bespoke joinery, finishes, technology, approvals, access and programme can materially change a project. Investigate them before narrowing the budget.

## Compare proposals fairly

Give tenderers the same brief and request the same breakdown. Record substitutions, provisional allowances, exclusions, programme assumptions and warranty terms. The lowest total is not necessarily the lowest complete project cost.

## Keep the forecast current

Use documented change control. Every approved change should show its effect on cost, timing and scope so the forecast remains useful.

Current pricing, availability and delivery capability must be confirmed for the actual project and location. Your Office Space assesses national fit-out briefs case by case.
